title: Affine realizability geometry uses raw W_enc, so the behaviorally null all-ones (mean) direction dominates c_free, kappa, c_qp, c_dec and enc_dec_cos in the primary GPT-2 setting
evidence: In the jb GPT-2 L6 SAE, every one of the 24576 W_enc columns has a positive component along 1/sqrt(d). The median |cos| with that direction is 0.73 (p99 0.82). The data never constrains this direction: training and analysis inputs are exactly mean-centred (HFModel.resid centres; TL center_writing_weights), so the component acts only as an extra bias. Every later read of the GPT-2 residual goes through a LayerNorm that subtracts the mean, so adding c*1 to the stream is exactly null for behavior (the HFModel docstring says so too). analyze_position_affine still uses J = W_enc^T at line 72/83 and gain = W_T.dhat at line 152, which lets edits exploit this null direction. I restricted edits to mean-zero deltas (W -> C W_enc, C = I - 11^T/d) on 16 cached-residual cases: kappa fell from 1.43 to 1.03, 1.59 to 1.02, 1.41 to 1.02, 1.20 to 1.01 and 1.38 to 1.02; c_free rose 30-90% (5.31 to 10.06); c_qp went from 5.33 to 6.67; c_dec went from 58.0 to 41.7 and from 36.1 to 26.9. With A non-empty, the artifact kappa is about 1/sqrt(1 - 0.73^2), roughly 1.46: c_free can use the 1-direction, but c_lin cannot, because every protected feature shares it. Caveat: the cases were per-text mean residuals from results/cache featstats, not per-position residuals, because GPT-2 was not run.
failure_scenario: 05_realizability.py on gpt2_relu_jb_L6 (real positions, L0 about 50). The pre-registered H2 diagnostics are then contaminated: median kappa, exact-QP cost, decoder collateral and the encoder-decoder-cosine baseline. The reported T/P 'interference' (kappa about 1.4-1.6) is mostly a property of the SAE's bias-like 1-direction, not of feature geometry the model can see. With the null direction removed, kappa is about 1.02, so H2 correlations and any 'interference exists' conclusion would be driven by an artifact, which is likely correlated with feature density, one of the H2 baselines. The same root cause likely affects enc/pinv/ridge/opt in methods.py: for K=1, pinv = enc puts about 53% of its norm-matched energy into the null direction. Their encoder self-consistency scores, measured on h + delta with its mean component, would also be spuriously good, which is exactly the 'encoder score improves but behavior does not' pattern the user wants to detect.
fix: For settings whose model is invariant to the residual mean (GPT-2 with centring; not Gemma/RMSNorm, and the LN TopK Jacobian already contains C), analyze the SAE on the canonical edited state C(h + delta). Use W = C @ W_enc in analyze_position_affine (or add the equality 1^T delta = 0 to Jeq), compute the dec gain with C @ dhat, and run the qp_check / dec collateral through sae.encode(center(h + x)) instead of pre + W^T x. Add a 'mean_invariant' flag to the setting and apply the same projection in methods.py Jacobians (pre_jacobian for norm='none') and in the internal metrics in evaluate.py. Re-run the realizability summary and the H2 diagnostics afterwards.

title: TopK+LN decoder cost comes from a coarse upward-only 1.25x line search: c_dec is overestimated (median 1.22x) and dec collateral is measured at the overshoot
evidence: Under LN, adding c*dhat inflates std, so the first-order c from rT/gain nearly always undershoots and the loop takes at least one multiplicative 1.25 step. On 96 TopK cases (cached per-text mean residuals, 16 concepts x K in {1,3} x 3), I bisected along dhat for the exact smallest c that reaches the target. c_dec divided by that minimum had median 1.22, mean 1.18 and max 1.25; 84% of cases were above 1.05. Because collateral is measured at the inflated c, dec_P_lost was inflated as well (reported vs exact-c: 10 vs 7, 19 vs 14, 12 vs 8, 10 vs 8). Other problems in the same block: success is tested on pre (p3[T] >= tau) rather than on activation (T must actually be in the top-k after the edit). If the loop never succeeds, dec_P_rel_change, dec_P_lost and dec_new_active are still written, evaluated at about 1.25^29 times the first-order scale, even though c_dec = inf; the affine path omits these fields in that case. A first-order gain <= 0 is also taken as unreachable, which is a local Taylor conclusion reported as a finite-step one.
failure_scenario: In the TopK robustness setting, the decoder-steering cost and collateral are systematically about 20% worse than the true values along the same direction. Meanwhile the GN solution is exact, so every 'dec vs constrained' cost/collateral comparison and the TopK H2 'decoder collateral' diagnostic are biased against dec. Any aggregate of dec collateral also mixes in the values from the huge failed scales.
fix: Bracket first (grow c until the true forward reaches the target at the activation level, i.e. f3[T] >= tau - tol with T in the top-k), then bisect to a relative tolerance of about 1e-4. Record collateral at the bisected c. When the target is not reachable within the bracket, set the collateral fields to NaN. Do not use the first-order gain sign as a reachability test under LN: always try the true forward along dhat.

title: Solver non-optimal statuses (user_limit, infeasible_inaccurate) and solver failures are reported as geometric infeasibility, and optimal_inaccurate is accepted as exact
evidence: In cvxpy 1.9.3, Clarabel MAX_ITERATIONS/MAX_TIME map to 'user_limit' with no exception, so there is no OSQP fallback. exact_qp returns None for every status except optimal/optimal_inaccurate, and analyze_position_affine (lines 127-136) then sets qp_feasible=False and c_qp=inf. Only an exception triggers the OSQP fallback, and an exception raised inside that fallback is not caught, which aborts the whole 05 run with no per-position guard. Constraint generation drops working-set constraints from the violation check (setdiff1d with work, line 117), so an inaccurate solve that violates a working constraint can still be declared converged.
failure_scenario: A badly scaled position, for example Gemma with pre about 850 and thresholds about 245, makes Clarabel stop at max_iter or return infeasible_inaccurate. The position is counted as 'not realizable' (c_qp=inf), which inflates the reported infeasibility fraction and the median exact-QP cost used in H2. Or a SolverError inside the OSQP fallback crashes the realizability script partway through a setting.
fix: Map only status == 'infeasible' to qp_feasible=False. For user_limit, *_inaccurate and solver errors, set qp_feasible=None (undetermined) and keep the status. Wrap the fallback in try/except. After the final round, check every accepted x against all (T, A, I) constraints with an explicit tolerance before setting qp_feasible=True. Consider scaling the problem (divide by |h|) for Gemma.

title: qp_within_budget is computed from a relaxation lower bound when constraint generation did not converge, and the last round's solution is never checked
evidence: If the loop ends at max_rounds, c_qp = ||x|| of the last relaxed QP, which is only a lower bound, and qp_feasible=None. qp_over_lin (line 148) and qp_within_budget (line 166) still use this lower bound, so qp_within_budget can be True for an undetermined case. The loop also solves on round max_rounds and exits without checking that solution for violations, so a feasible final solution is reported as not converged.
failure_scenario: Large edits at positions where more than 60x48 inactive constraints are needed. These are rare given the observed 2-3-round convergence, but most likely at large Delta or K=3. They get counted as 'realizable within budget' while unresolved, which biases the within-budget fraction upward.
fix: Run one more violation check after the loop. Set qp_within_budget (and qp_over_lin) to None when qp_feasible is None, or report them only for converged cases.

title: The jb ReLU SAE's Jacobian is dominated by the all-ones direction, which GPT-2 ignores, so the constrained methods only look constrained
evidence:
Measured on jb gpt2-small-res-jb L6 (weights from hf_cache). For every one of the 24576 W_enc columns, the component along 1/sqrt(d) is positive, with a median of 73% of the column norm. The top singular value of W_enc is 318; the next is 28.8. The SAE was trained on centred residuals (TransformerLens center_writing_weights; the HF hook also centres h), so this direction was never constrained.

In GPT-2 the direction has no effect, because every read of the residual stream goes through a LayerNorm. I checked this with HFModel(layer=5, center=True): adding 50*1/sqrt(d) at every position changed the logits by at most 6e-5. A centred random edit of norm 5 changed them by 3.9.

pre_jacobian with norm=='none' returns the raw W_enc rows (lines 148-149, via pre() at lines 88-92). As a result, pinv, ridge, *_fs, dec_proj_randP and opt (methods.py 191-227, 259-288) meet J_P delta=0 and the finite-step constraints partly by moving along 1. Results on 21 real positions, alpha = 0.45 x median norm, raw vs mean-removed delta:
- pinv: pRel 0.000 and 0 lost features, vs 0.27-0.31 and 24-28 lost per position.
- pinv_fs / dec_proj_fs: 1-3 new active features and pRel 0, vs 54-91 new and pRel 0.37-0.57. That is worse than dec, which has pRel 0.33-0.36.
- The mean component that causes this is only about 1-1.5 norm units out of 35.

The same root cause affects realizability.py:77 (W = sae.W_enc). There kappa is 1.41-1.63 raw vs 1.07-1.09 with a centred encoder, and c_free is about 30% too low.
failure_scenario: This affects the dev1 sweep now running on gpt2_relu_jb_L6 and the realizability/H2 analysis. The run would report that pinv, *_fs and opt preserve the protected features exactly and remove new activations, and that this internal success does not carry over to behaviour. That dissociation would be an artefact: along the directions the model can actually see, the corrected edits change protected features as much as dec or more. The H2 diagnostics (median kappa, QP cost) would also be inflated by a direction the model ignores. Both H1 and H2 conclusions could flip.
fix:
For SAEs trained on centred residuals (the jb setting; add a flag from pinned.json):
- Centre the input inside SAEWrap.pre (x = h - h.mean(-1)).
- Make pre_jacobian return centred rows (W - W.mean over d) for norm=='none'.
- Project every method's delta onto 1-perp before norm matching.
- Use the centred W_enc in realizability.analyze_position_affine.

Then re-run the dev sweep and the realizability analysis. Leave Gemma (RMSNorm) and the OAI LayerNorm SAE unchanged.

title: enc is not really norm-matched: 51-70% of its squared norm is along the all-ones direction
evidence:
g_T = sum_t w_t W_enc[:,t] with raw jb columns. On 21 real positions, 51-70% of ||delta||^2 lies along 1/sqrt(d), with a mean component of +25 to +27 at alpha = 0.45 x median norm (35.5). The effective (centred) norm is therefore only 0.55-0.70 x alpha. The internal numbers are inflated as well:
- tgt_gain 49.4 raw vs 21.6 with the mean removed (topic:5, K=1).
- new_active 24528 per position (every feature) vs 356-867.
- pRel 9.1-9.8 vs 0.55-0.73.
The pilot log shows the same thing (enc new=24514).
failure_scenario: When enc is compared with dec, diffmean and the others at the same alpha grid (up to 0.9), it is actually running at roughly 0.6x strength. Its behavioural dose-response and its alpha chosen on dev are therefore biased. Its internal scores are the largest of any method only because of the ignored direction, which feeds a false 'internal gain without behaviour' pattern for the encoder-gradient baseline.
fix: Use centred encoder rows (this follows from the saes.py fix), or at least set delta <- delta - delta.mean(-1) and renormalise to alpha, whenever the SAE and model live in centred coordinates.

title: Internal metrics are computed on h+delta without removing the mean, so a tiny ignored component dominates them
evidence:
_collect encodes h + delta as is, but the model is invariant to delta's all-ones component and the jb encoder is very sensitive to it (about 2 units of pre-activation per unit of mean component, for every feature). On 21 real positions at alpha = 0.45, raw vs mean-removed delta:
- dec: 16-38 lost and 17-19 new per position, vs 7-20 lost and 69-99 new.
- random: new_active 49.5 or 2720 depending only on the sign of random_dir's mean component (-0.90 vs +3.28, which varies by concept seed). After centring it is 66-157.
- ridge: 3552-4224 new vs 97-356.
err_norm_ratio and err_delta_frac (lines 319-323) have the same problem.
failure_scenario: The 'encoder self-consistency' arm (int_tgt_gain, int_p_rel_change, int_new_active_per_pos, int_err_*) is used in the NO_GO rule ('improvements only in encoder metrics') and to contrast internal scores with behaviour. These numbers mostly reflect how much of each method's delta falls along 1 and with what sign, not collateral damage the model can see. Method rankings on internal metrics, including dec vs random vs the constrained methods, can reverse.
fix: Measure internal metrics on the canonical representation. For centred-coordinate settings, compute pre2, f2 = sae.encode_full(h + (delta - delta.mean(-1, keepdim=True))), or centre inside SAEWrap.pre as in the saes.py fix. Report the fraction of ||delta||^2 along 1 as a diagnostic.

title: opt's fixed candidate set misses almost every feature that opt actually turns on, so the new-activation penalty does nothing
evidence:
The candidates are a fixed top-512 by |d_T.W_enc| + |g_T.W_enc|/||W_enc||. Because of operator precedence, only the second term is normalised. That term is dominated by the shared all-ones component: median 0.85 vs 0.056 for the decoder term. The resulting candidates barely overlap with those from a centred encoder (77-123 of 512).

On 21 real positions (jb, alpha = 0.45), only 0.06-0.2% of the features opt newly activates are in the candidate set. Even with a centred W, only 2-6% of dec's newly activated features would be. Because the penalty relu(pre - thr) is applied only to candidates, the mu_new term has almost no effect. opt ends with 117-338 new features per position, vs 17-19 for dec (raw metric).
failure_scenario: 'opt' is meant to be the direct activation-optimisation baseline (task item 3). In practice it optimises target gain under the linear P projection and ignores collateral activation. So opt vs the linear/fs methods (and any 'direct optimisation doesn't help' conclusion) compares against a strawman, not the stated objective.

title: Internal-vs-behavior Spearman pools all alphas, so steering strength drives it rather than internal quality
evidence: `cc = tab[tab.method.isin([...SAE methods...])]` holds one row per (method, alpha, K). `spearmanr(cc['int_tgt_gain'], cc['dC'])` then runs over 8 methods x 6 alphas x 2 K. Both int_tgt_gain and dC rise with alpha (see the pilot log). Within one alpha the relationship is reversed. In logs_pilot_relu.txt at alpha=1, topic:5: enc tgt=90.9 gives C=0.774, pinv 38.6 gives 0.991, dec 23.7 gives 0.994, dec_proj_fs 13.6 gives 0.991. For emotion:1: enc 77.6 gives 0.432, pinv 41.5 gives 0.321, dec 27.0 gives 0.613, dec_proj_fs 17.8 gives 0.751.
failure_scenario: summary.json reports a large positive `tgt_gain_vs_dC` rho. The reader concludes that encoder self-consistency gains carry over to behavior (research step 8). At matched norm, though, the methods with the highest internal target gain (enc, pinv) have the lowest judge dC. The pooled statistic hides exactly the internal-only improvement that the protocol defines as NO_GO. `p_rel_change_vs_dNLL` and `new_active_vs_dNLL` have the same confound.
fix: Compute the correlation within each alpha (and K) across methods and concepts, then report the per-alpha rho and a pooled stratified estimate. Alternatively, correlate residuals after regressing out alpha, or correlate at the dev-selected operating points only. Pair at (cid, alpha) level, not on concept-averaged table rows. Drop the pooled-over-alpha rho or label it as confounded.

title: Aggregation, selection and the H1 bootstrap key only on (method, alpha, K); other hyper-parameter variants are silently averaged
evidence: condition_table groups by ('method','alpha','K') plus cid. budget_select groups by ('method','K'). 11_decide.subset filters on method/K/alpha only. cluster_bootstrap_diff uses `pivot_table(index='cid', columns='prompt')`, whose default aggfunc is mean. per_prompt_frame never records max_density at all. 04_sweep applies grid['extra'] (protect_topm, ridge_rel, fs_rounds, opt_mu_*, max_density) to every SAE method. Toy check: ridge rows with ridge_rel=0.1 (dC=1) and ridge_rel=1.0 (dC=0) in one frame gave cluster_bootstrap_diff est=0.5, with no warning.
failure_scenario: The protocol says ridge lambda and the P rule (protect_topm) are chosen on dev. Suppose a second dev part, or a test part, in the same run directory runs `extra={'ridge_rel':0.1}` or `{'protect_topm':32}`. Then table.csv, budget_select, the frozen alpha and the held-out H1 bootstrap all average across configurations that were never meant to be pooled. The selected alpha, PRIMARY_CORRECTED and the GO estimate then refer to a mixture, not to any single method.
fix: Carry every Condition field, including max_density, into the frame and group by all of them (or by a config id = hash of the Condition minus cid). Have protocol.json freeze the full config. In cluster_bootstrap_diff use `df.pivot(...)`, which raises on duplicates, or assert that each (cid, prompt) cell appears exactly once per arm. Assert uniqueness in 11_decide.subset.

title: Condition.key and the score cache carry no code or config fingerprint; the dev1 sweep is running on pre-fix methods/saes code
evidence: The key hashes only Condition fields. It excludes EditSpec defaults (opt_steps, fs_max_add, opt_lr...), seed, max_new_tokens, prompt set and code version. done_keys (04_sweep.py:40,51) skips any matching key. score_rows (evaluate.py:150-159) reuses cached scores by key without checking the continuations. The running sweep processes (PIDs 12283/12284) started at 15:51. src/n3/methods.py, saes.py, settings.py and realizability.py were modified at 16:15-16:16: center_input/center_delta norm matching, opt_steps 25->20, and a rewritten _opt. The live processes therefore produce results with the old code.
failure_scenario: (a) Suppose dev1 is interrupted and resumed, or more parts are appended to it. The file then silently mixes rows from two implementations of the methods: norm matching with vs without the 1-direction, and a different opt. (b) Dev selections (alpha per method, PRIMARY_CORRECTED, B_NLL) taken from dev1 were made on the old implementation but get transferred to held-out runs on the new one. (c) Suppose a run's .jsonl is regenerated after a bug fix while its .scores.jsonl remains. 06_score then reuses stale judge scores for the new generations, and 07/11 analyze mismatched scores. (d) A resumed part with a different concepts[0] appends a second 'none' baseline, and the assert at 07_analyze.py:35 aborts.
fix: Put in every row a code fingerprint (git rev plus a hash of src/n3/*.py) and the full EditSpec/generation config (seed, max_new_tokens, prompt-list hash). Include them in the key, or refuse to resume when they differ. Store sha1(conts) in each score record and re-score on mismatch. Use a cid-independent key for the 'none' baseline. Treat dev1 as produced by the old code: re-run it, or freeze protocol.json from a dev run made with the exact code used for held-out. Make done_keys/load_rows tolerate a truncated last line.

title: Two-way percentile cluster bootstrap over only 8 held-out concepts is anti-conservative for the primary GO test
evidence: The held-out set has 8 concepts (5 topic + 3 emotion), resampled with replacement without stratification, and GO is read from percentile bounds or the 2*min-tail p-value. Simulation (scratchpad sim_boot.py, 300 null replicates, 8x48 design, the same resampling as cluster_bootstrap_diff): when between-concept heterogeneity of the paired difference dominates (sd_c=0.10, sd_e=0.10), type-I rate = 0.103 at nominal 0.05. With sd_c=0.10, sd_p=0.02, sd_e=0.20 it is 0.077. The percentile bootstrap uses an n (not n-1) variance and normal-like quantiles, while the effective df is about 7.
failure_scenario: The corrected method's per-concept advantage over dec varies strongly across concepts, which is likely because several concepts sit at the C≈0.99 ceiling. The lower 95% bound then excludes 0 about twice as often as nominal under a true null, which inflates false H1 GO.
fix: Make the primary inference concept-level. Options: an exact sign-flip randomization test on the 8 per-concept mean differences (2^8 flips), a t-test with 7 df, or a mixed model with concept and prompt random effects. Stratify resampling by family. Keep the two-way bootstrap as a sensitivity analysis. Pre-register the choice in protocol.json.

title: Fluency budget and GO fluency guard use only Qwen dNLL, which repetition/degeneration can game; dDist2 is measured but never used
evidence: budget_select filters `sub[cost] <= budget` with cost='dNLL'. 11_decide's guard uses dNLL (and dRel/protJS/dce), never dDist2. Conditional NLL of a continuation drops sharply once the text starts copying itself (e.g. dec_proj a=1: "stadium's stadium in the stadium"), whereas gibberish-type failures (enc/pinv at a=1) raise NLL.
failure_scenario: Methods whose failure mode is repetition, typically decoder-direction methods at high alpha, pass the dNLL budget at larger alpha and get a high judge dC for keyword spam. Methods whose failure mode is token soup are held to small alpha. This biases the dev-selected operating points and the held-out H1 comparison in favor of repetition-prone methods.
fix: Add a degeneration constraint (e.g. mean dDist2 >= -tau, or a repetition rate) to budget_select and to the GO guard. Alternatively, use a fluency score that penalizes repetition (e.g. NLL on de-duplicated text or an LLM fluency rating). Report matched-dDist2 results.

title: budget_select never treats alpha=0 as a candidate, and a missing arm yields p_two_sided=0.0 with NaN estimate
evidence: alpha=0 is returned only when no alpha is feasible. When every feasible alpha has negative dC, the best negative alpha is chosen (toy check: method m chose alpha=0.1 with dC=-0.02). A fallback alpha=0 has no rows in any sweep, because the sweep only runs 'none' at alpha 0. With an empty arm, cluster_bootstrap_diff returns est=nan and p_two_sided=0.0 (verified), since NaN boots count as neither <=0 nor >=0. The fallback row also has NaN for dRel/protJS/dce, and if every config falls back, 07_analyze.py:54 raises KeyError.
failure_scenario: If protocol.json freezes alpha=0 for a comparator (e.g. no diffmean alpha meets a tight B_NLL), 11_decide gets an empty subset. It reports p=0 for that comparison, which Holm counts as the first rejection, loosening the threshold for the other comparator to 0.05. The missing arm is not flagged. If the primary is empty, `L[prim]` raises KeyError.
fix: Include alpha=0 (dC=0, dNLL=0) explicitly as a candidate in budget_select, or document that it is excluded. In cluster_bootstrap_diff, raise when either arm is empty or D is all NaN, and use nan-aware p (ignore NaN boots, return NaN). In 11_decide, assert that every selected arm has n_concepts x n_prompts rows.

title: Runtime metric charges dec/enc for a full SAE encode they do not need
evidence: In _edit_chunk, every non-generic method runs `pre, f = sae.encode_full(h)` inside the timed block before `_sae_method`, including dec (a constant direction) and enc (a constant Jacobian for norm='none'). dev1 rows show ms_per_pos: diffmean 0.006, dec 0.32-0.34, enc 0.33, pinv ~1.0, *_fs 4-5.7, opt 7.5.
failure_scenario: The reported runtime overhead of the constrained methods relative to decoder steering (the runtime part of step 7) is understated by roughly 50x. For example, pinv looks 3x dec when the true ratio is about 170x, and dec looks 50x more expensive than diffmean although both are a constant vector add.
fix: Compute encode_full only for methods that need pre/f (move it inside `_sae_method` per branch), or time the method-specific work separately from the shared encode used by `_collect`. Report runtime on an otherwise idle CPU, since the two sweep processes currently contend.

title: Implemented H1 decision rule diverges from the pre-registered protocol
evidence: docs/02_protocol.md §6: GO = lower 95% bound > 0 against dec and diffmean, plus the held-out dNLL guard (0.1 nats). NO_GO also if the method is indistinguishable from diffmean/random. The code instead uses (i) Holm-adjusted bootstrap p-values, (ii) an extra `collateral_not_worse_than_dec` gate with unregistered tolerances (protJS +0.01, dce +0.05, dRel -0.02), and (iii) no comparison against `random`.
failure_scenario: Outcomes where the protocol says GO but the code says NO_GO (or vice versa) are possible. An example is a CI bound > 0 with p slightly above 0.025, or dce 0.06 above dec. Tolerances chosen after the protocol text but before or while viewing data weaken the pre-registration claim.
fix: Put the exact rule (Holm or not, collateral gates and their tolerances, the random comparator) in configs/protocol.json and the protocol doc before any test_* run, and make 11_decide read these values from protocol.json rather than hard-coding them.

title: Concept texts for feature selection and DiffMean are the primary judges' fine-tuning data
evidence: concept_texts samples yahoo_answers_topics train shard 0 and dair-ai/emotion train. fabriceyhc/bert-base-uncased-yahoo_answers_topics and bhadresh-savani/distilbert-base-uncased-emotion were fine-tuned on those same train splits. The protocol calls the judges independent and only notes that they are validated on the test splits.
failure_scenario: The steering directions (DiffMean especially, and T selection) are fit to the same dataset-specific cues the judge learned. dC then partly measures alignment with judge-training artifacts rather than the concept. Methods using the concept texts more directly (diffmean) get an advantage, which can shift the H1 comparison.
fix: Take concept texts from data the judges did not see (e.g. part of the test splits not used for judge validation, or another corpus), or make the NLI judge a co-primary endpoint with a concordance requirement. At minimum, disclose the overlap in the protocol.

title: H2 outcome pools dev-concept dC (dev prompts, alpha tuned on these very outcomes) with held-out-concept dC (held-out prompts)
evidence: The outcome for the 8 dev concepts comes from the dev run (24 prompts, the alpha that maximized mean dev dC under the budget). The outcome for the 8 held-out concepts comes from the test run (48 different prompts, different baseline C0). Spearman over 16 concepts takes no account of the split.
failure_scenario: A systematic dev-vs-held-out shift in dC can manufacture or mask a |rho| >= 0.5 across 16 points. Sources are winner's-curse inflation on dev and prompt-set differences in the baseline. This can happen whenever the diagnostic happens to differ between the two concept groups.
fix: Evaluate all 16 concepts on the same prompt set at the frozen alpha (e.g. run dev concepts on held-out prompts), or compute the correlation within split and combine, with a split indicator or partial Spearman.

title: Gemma generation on ragged, left-padded prompt batches: pads are attended and the BOS is edited, because the mask is all ones and only column 0 is skipped
evidence:
- The Gemma tokenizer (unsloth/gemma-3-270m, pinned snapshot) has padding_side='left' and add_bos_token=True, and HFModel.to_tokens calls it with padding=True (line 132).
- With the frozen splits, 23 of 24 dev prompts and 47 of 48 test prompts are padded: dev is (24, 17) with lengths 11-17, test is (48, 20) with lengths 9-20. Column 0 is <pad>=0 in every padded row, and BOS=2 sits at a later column.
- 04_sweep.py explicitly skips its equal-length assert for gemma settings.
- HFModel.generate (line 202) then passes attention_mask=torch.ones_like(tokens), so the pad tokens are attended as real context and BOS is no longer at position 0.
- _EditState.apply (line 37) skips only column 0 on the prefill call. For padded rows that column is a pad, so the BOS position (the attention sink) and the remaining pad positions are edited.
- Synthetic check: a tiny Gemma3ForCausalLM with the same left-padding layout changed last-token logits by 0.034 with pads attended. The prefill editor call received every row's positions 1..s-1, including BOS and pads.
- The GPT-2 path is unaffected: manual BOS and equal-length prompts give 6 edited positions on prefill and exactly 1 per later step.
failure_scenario: The Gemma-3-270m / Gemma Scope 2 behavioral run (the cross-model, cross-SAE held-out setting, run if the primary result is GO) generates from '<pad>...<pad><bos> prompt'. Every method's edit is applied to the BOS residual and to the pads. H-dependent methods (pinv, dec_proj, *_fs, opt) compute very different deltas there than dec or diffmean do, so the behavioral differences between methods are confounded by edits to the attention sink. The unedited baseline is also degraded by attended pads. The internal metrics (positions, tgt_gain, p_rel_change, err_*) average in BOS and pad positions. Any conclusion that results generalize, or fail to generalize, to Gemma is invalid.
fix: Do not batch ragged prompts. Either group prompts by Gemma token length, or generate one prompt at a time. Alternatively, return the tokenizer's attention_mask from to_tokens and pass it to generate, and give _EditState a per-row skip mask on the prefill call. The mask should exclude every position where attention_mask==0 and each row's BOS, not just column 0. Also assert that no row's BOS is edited.

title: The prompting-reference cue inserts a second BOS for Gemma and anchors on column 0, which is a pad under left padding
evidence: prompt_tokens_with_cue builds its cue with model.tokenizer(PROMPT_CUE.format(name) + '\n'), and the Gemma tokenizer adds <bos> by default (tok('hi') -> [2, 2202]). It then concatenates prompt_tokens[:, :1], the cue, and prompt_tokens[:, 1:]. With left padding, column 0 is <pad> for 23 of 24 dev rows. The result looks like '<pad> <bos> This is a story about X.\n <pad>... <bos> prompt'. For GPT-2 (no auto-BOS, manual BOS at column 0) this is correct.
failure_scenario: In the Gemma setting, the 'prompt' reference condition used to benchmark activation steering sees a double or mid-sequence BOS and interleaved pads. This lowers its concept score and fluency, so the steering methods look better relative to prompting than they really are.
fix: Tokenize the cue with add_special_tokens=False, insert it right after each row's BOS (not after column 0), and build prompts without padding, as in the fix above.

title: The HF-vs-TL backend check only uses an h-independent edit (dec) under teacher forcing; it never tests the editor-input centering or the KV-cache generate path
evidence:
The edited-logits comparison uses EditSpec('dec', ...), a constant direction, so the delta does not depend on the h that _EditState.apply passes to the editor. If the centering at models.py:42-43 were wrong or missing, the check would still pass for dec, but pinv, dec_proj, *_fs, opt, and enc for the LN-normalized TopK SAE would silently diverge from TL coordinates. The script also never calls generate, so the calls>0 branch (BOS skip only on the prefill, one edit per new position under the KV cache) is not covered. By reasoning and a tiny random-weight GPT-2 check, I found no current discrepancy:
- Prefill edited b*(s-1) rows, then exactly b rows per step.
- Adding c*1 to delta changed log-probs by less than 1e-6, confirming ln_f invariance.
- The resid match (rel 1e-6) implies that the editor inputs match.
So this is a gap in evidence, not a live bug.
failure_scenario: A future change to _EditState or HFModel (for example, dropping center=True or changing the hook output handling) that breaks h-dependent methods or generation in the primary GPT-2 setting would still pass this validation, while the protocol cites it as proof that the HF backend equals TransformerLens.
fix: Also compare HF vs TL edited log-probs for an h-dependent method, such as pinv or dec_proj_fs with the jb SAE and enc with the OAI SAE, and assert that the editor inputs match. Add a short greedy (do_sample=False) generate comparison of a few tokens between the TL and HF backends with a recording editor, asserting identical tokens and per-call edited-position counts.
